text:
ConocoPhillips fell 1.66% today to $144.40, giving back gains from a sharp rally earlier in the week. The stock peaked at $154.03 on October 30th but has retreated $9.63 since then—a move driven primarily by crude oil prices cooling over the past two days. US oil fell from elevated levels as markets priced in hopes for a diplomatic resolution to the Iran conflict, reducing fears of major supply disruptions that had briefly pushed prices higher.

The broader context matters here: oil companies benefit when crude prices are high and rising, but they suffer when prices fall and uncertainty about geopolitical risk starts to ease. Yesterday's U.S. military strikes on Iran's Qeshm Island did not prevent oil from declining, and signals of openness to negotiation from both sides have now weighed on energy stocks more than geopolitical risk premiums have supported them. Separately, news about Democratic gains in the midterms could add longer-term headwinds for traditional energy companies if it leads to policy favoring renewables over oil and gas.
